name: Zedekiah
overview: Zedekiah was a male member of the tribe of Judah, uniquely identified as the son of Eliakim, also known as Jehoiakim, as recorded in 1 Chronicles 3:16. His role and life are significant within the historical and prophetic context of Judah's monarchy.
namesAndTitles: The name Zedekiah means 'YHWH is [my] righteousness,' reflecting a proper name given to him, though not directly by God, as noted in 1 Chronicles 3:16. This name highlights a divine attribute connected to his identity.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Zedekiah as the son of Eliakim, also called Jehoiakim, according to 1 Chronicles 3:16. Beyond this paternal link, no additional family relationships are detailed in the provided facts.
scriptureSignificance: Zedekiah's biblical importance lies in his position as a king of Judah who, despite warnings from the prophet Jeremiah, struggled with indecision and fear of his officials. His rebellion against Babylon led to devastating consequences for Jerusalem, including its destruction and the loss of his sons, culminating in his own captivity. His story serves as a solemn example of the repercussions of weak leadership and the failure to obey God's prophetic counsel.

keyEvents.event: Sons killed, eyes blinded, taken to Babylon
